oneLineSummary: Multi-agent concurrent KG writes need HLC+Or-Set CRDT to preserve causal order & reference integrity without data loss.
rootCause: Lamport timestamps alone cannot detect concurrency; state-based merges lose edits (LWW collision). Multi-agent simultaneous reference writes → last-write-wins silently drops intermediate updates. KG Longinus binders (sourceId+sourcePath) lack causal tracking → dangling or stale references in merged states.
recommendation: Adopt Hybrid Logical Clock (HLC) + Or-Set CRDT: (1) Replace Lamport with HLC (wall-ms + counter + node_id) for monotonic physical-time guarantees. (2) Wrap KG references as Or-Set entries (tag=(agent_id, seq)) → concurrent add+remove → add wins via tag identity. (3) On KG merge: apply Or-Set causal semantics (remove only observed tags) before state application. (4) Persist HLC state on each agent for recovery across sessions.

technicalDetails.hlcComponent: 16 bytes: u64 wall_ms + u32 counter + u32 node_id. tick() increments counter; recv(remote) → max(local.counter, remote.counter)+1. Preserves causal ordering: if a→b (a send then recv), then hlc(a) < hlc(b).
technicalDetails.orSetApplication: Each KG reference triple (entity_id, sourceId, sourcePath) tagged as Or-Set entry. Tag = (agent_id, sequence). Concurrent edits: Agent A adds {ref1, tag_A_1} && Agent B removes {ref1, tag_A_1} → merge favors add (tag not yet tombstoned on B's side). Delta sync: only transmit new (value,tag) pairs and removal tags, not full state.
technicalDetails.stateVectorPiggybacking: SyncPayload includes per-agent max HLC seen. On receive: if remote.hlc > local.hlc for that agent, apply delta; else discard (already seen). Prevents out-of-order delivery bugs.
technicalDetails.mergeSemantics: State-based Or-Set: merge_delta(remote_delta) applies removes first (tombstone tags), then adds (skip if already tombstoned). Idempotent, commutative, associative. For KG: each MERGE operation in Neo4j → wrap in Or-Set semantics before APOC merge.
technicalDetails.333SignalingIntegration: WebRTC DataChannel carries postcard-encoded SyncPayload with HLC. Leader sends snapshot (full state + HLC vector). Peers apply deltas with causal checks. Late joiner catches up: snapshot + committed blocks (BFT view guarantees total order for consensus txns).

alternatives.name: Vector Clock
alternatives.tradeoff: Precise causality detection (O(n) storage per message). Overkill for LWW maps; better for detecting ALL concurrency but slower merge checks. Use if causal conflict detection critical.
alternatives.when: When you need to detect "were A and B concurrent?" for every pair. Kubernetes Optimistic Locking uses vector-like logic.

alternatives.name: Last-Writer-Wins (LWW) without HLC
alternatives.tradeoff: Current 333 approach: Lamport timestamp + node_id tiebreak. Silent data loss if concurrent edits to same KG reference. Suitable for game state (blocks override each other) but NOT for KG integrity.
alternatives.when: Only if you can tolerate lost updates on collision. Not recommended for immutable Longinus references.

alternatives.name: Operational Transform (OT)
alternatives.tradeoff: Complex transform functions for each data type. Works for text (Google Docs) but hard to generalize to KG triples.
alternatives.when: Real-time text collaboration. Not practical for structured KG data.

references: Shapiro 2011: A Comprehensive Study of CRDT (state-based Or-Set definition, merge semantics)
Kulkarni 2014: Logical Physical Clocks and Consistent Snapshots in Distributed Systems (HLC invention, monotonicity proof)
Kleppmann 2017: Automerge: Real-time Collaborative Editing Without Operational Transformation (state vector + delta optimization)
Attiya 2016: Replicated Data Types for Geo-Replicated Transactional Systems (RGA ordered list CRDT)
333 Platform src: or_set.rs (Observed-Remove Set impl), lww_map.rs (LWW-Map with Lamport), sync.rs (delta batching, state vector), lamport.rs (current Lamport clock)
expectedKGImpact: Eliminates silent data loss on concurrent reference writes. Agents can merge KG snapshots without coordination → no dangling Longinus binders. 333 signaling distributes CRDT state safely over WebRTC with HLC causality. Enables multi-agent APT workflows (SA, SP, ST, SCW in parallel) with guaranteed reference consistency.
implementationPriority: PHASE 1: Add HLC to 333-platform/src/hlc.rs (ready: CONTRACT_333_HLC exists). PHASE 2: Extend Or-Set to wrap KG (entity_id, sourceId, sourcePath) tuples. PHASE 3: Integrate HLC+Or-Set into KG MERGE operations (Cypher MERGE → wrap in Or-Set pre/post hooks). PHASE 4: End-to-end test: 3 agents write concurrent KG updates → verify zero data loss on merge.
riskMitigation: Clock skew: HLC tolerates skew ≤ 1 second (wall_ms has 1ms precision, counter as tiebreak). If system clocks drift >1s, HLC logical counter still maintains causality.

Tombstone growth: Or-Set accumulates tombstones indefinitely. Mitigate via epoch-based GC (all peers acknowledge epoch → safe to GC) or time-based (>7 days old = remove). 333 already has gc_epoch() & gc_time() in or_set.rs.
Network partitions: HLC continues ticking on both sides independently. On reconnect, max(A.hlc, B.hlc)+1 resumes consensus. State vector + delta sync ensures no duplicate application.
Byzantine agents: HLC+Or-Set does NOT prevent Byzantine attacks (agent lies about HLC). Requires BFT consensus (HotStuff in 333) for commit finality. Use HLC for CRDT layer, BFT for ordering layer.

conclusion: HLC + Or-Set CRDT is the proven approach for multi-agent distributed reference writes. 333 Platform already has Lamport + Or-Set code. Upgrade path: Lamport→HLC (add wall-ms), confirm SyncPayload piggybacks state vector, wrap KG references as Or-Set entries. This unblocks multi-agent APT workflows and 333 P2P consensus.
